subject: Next steps: deployment mode & dedicated GPU mix for DeltaHealth POC
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@deltahealth.com>, Sasha Lee <sasha.lee@deltahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Recap & immediate asks — deployment mode discussion + sizing clarifications

Alex / Sasha — thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and the small set of clarifying asks so we can land a clean Dedicated POC proposal.

Recap (high level)
- Primary goal: integrate Redwood inference for clinical-notes summarization and patient-facing chat for a 3-month POC.
- Required SLA targets: p95 latency sub-350ms for short-turn chats (<= 250 tokens).
- Data posture: PHI-in-scope for inference; customer prefers VPC/private deployment but open to Dedicated in our isolated tenant if KMS integration is acceptable.

Clarifying asks (to confirm before we size):
1) Expected sustained TPS (requests/sec) during business hours vs peak burst. You mentioned ~80 TPS sustained with 250 TPS peaks — can you confirm exact windows?
2) Average request token mix (prompt tokens vs generated tokens). A sample distribution like 80% prompts < 150 tokens and 20% generation <= 300 tokens is helpful.
3) Concurrency expectations per user/session (do you expect multi-turn sessions to maintain KV cache across bursts?).
4) Network constraints for a VPC/on-prem option (eg egress rules, proxy details) — Sasha, can you share the rough networking constraints?

Next steps — what we'll deliver after your answers
- Draft Dedicated capacity worksheet with GPU flavor options (A10G / H100 / L4x2 mixes) and TPS-to-GPU mapping.
- If VPC preferred, include private deployment checklist + KMS/HSM integration notes.
- Pricing & timeline for a 3-month POC with canary rollout plan.

Can we get the answers to 1–3 by EOD Friday PST? If not, a quick slack or 15-min sync early next week will suffice.

Thanks — Priyom
--
Priyom Das

From: Alex Mercer <alex@deltahealth.com>

Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & immediate asks — deployment mode discussion + sizing clarifications

Priyom — thanks for the writeup; looks right. Quick answers inline below.

1) TPS: baseline autoscaled traffic during business hours (8am-6pm PST) ~ 70–90 TPS. Typical daily peaks spike to ~200–260 TPS for ~20–40 minutes (batch notifications + shift-change). Outside business hours we see <15 TPS.
2) Token mix: approx 75% of requests are short prompts (median prompt tokens ~120) with small completions (median generation 80 tokens). The remaining 25% are longer summarization jobs: prompt ~800 tokens, generation ~120 tokens.
3) Concurrency: we want session-level KV cache for multi-turn clinical workflows; active concurrent sessions ~4 per clinician during peak but the per-request concurrency to the model is what matters for GPU sizing. Peak concurrent in-flight requests across the system ~220–250.
4) Sasha will follow up on network constraints; for Dedicated we need to understand whether private peering is required.

Happy to jump on a short call if any of this is unclear.

—Alex
Alex Mercer
CTO, DeltaHealth
alex@deltahealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Alex Mercer <alex@deltahealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 18:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & immediate asks — deployment mode discussion + sizing clarifications

Thanks Alex — useful numbers. A few immediate sizing thoughts and a question on quality tradeoffs:

- Given 70–90 sustained TPS and 200–260 peak bursts, Dedicated with autoscaling + burst buffer looks appropriate if you want predictable latency and data isolation. Private VPC could be used but adds ~2–3 week infra setup depending on networking.
- Initial GPU flavor candidates: 2x H100 (for low latency, large context; better for the long summarize jobs) paired with several L4x2 nodes for high-concurrency, short-turn chat. H100 nodes handle KV heavy multi-turn sessions; L4x2 provide better cost/TPS for short completions.
- Estimated baseline footprint (very rough): 2 H100 + 4 L4x2 to start. That maps to ~140–180 sustained TPS with headroom for bursts using autoscale + burst pool. We'll refine once we see token distribution histograms.

Question: for the summarization batch jobs (prompt ~800 tokens), are you tolerant of slightly higher p95 (eg up to 600ms) if it reduces cost compared to running all summarization on H100? If yes, we can route summarization to quantized variants and reserve H100 for low-latency interactive chat.

I'll let Ben run the capacity worksheet and produce a first-pass estimate. Neha — can you confirm if DeltaHealth prefers KMS integration in Dedicated or if the initial POC can use Redwood-managed keys (we'll mark PHI boundaries accordingly)?

-Marissa
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Mercer <alex@deltahealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & immediate asks — deployment mode discussion + sizing clarifications

Adding the first-pass capacity worksheet (attached) and a suggested routing policy. Attachment: DeltaHealth_capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet) — includes three scenarios: conservative (cost-optimized), balanced, performance-first.

Highlights from the Balanced scenario:
- GPUs: 2 x H100 (48GB) + 4 x L4x2 (NVIDIA L4x2 equivalent)
- Sustained TPS headroom: ~160–190 TPS depending on token mix; burst pool can handle 240–280 TPS for short windows if autoscale triggers extra L4x2 instances quickly (30–90s spin-up).
- Concurrency mapping: we assume 1.2 in-flight requests per TPS on average due to multi-turn KV cache; we size for 1.4 to be safe.
- Token budget: assume median 120 prompt + 80 gen for 75% requests; 800+120 for long jobs. Cost and latency numbers in the worksheet.

Notes on routing and fallbacks:
- Route interactive chat to L4x2 quantized models with eviction fallback to H100 for cache-warm sessions where strict latency required.
- Longer summarization jobs routed to H100 unless customer accepts quantized run on L4x2 (lower cost, higher latency).

Attachment 2 (network diagram) is referenced in the Drive link in my email to Priyom.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Next steps & proposed timeline — DeltaHealth POC (3 months)

Alex / Sasha — attaching the balanced worksheet and the network diagram (links below) — summary of next steps so we have one canonical plan: 

1) DeltaHealth to confirm: (a) whether KMS-managed keys required for POC or Redwood-managed keys acceptable, (b) approval on the balanced scenario GPU mix (2H100 + 4L4x2) or preference for performance-first. Target: EOD Mon PST.
2) If Dedicated accepted: Redwood to provide an onboarding checklist for VPC peering / private routes; Sasha to share any network constraints. Target: 5 business days after confirmation.
3) Contract & procurement: preliminary SOW and 3-month reserved capacity quote will be shared once GPU mix agreed. Procurement cc'd for tracking.
4) Kickoff & telemetry: bench tests and a 48-hour soak to validate p95 latency and token-cost estimates.
